anchor_definition: The anchor is the `login` function whose body assembles the request payload r — setting password (and phone/countryCode) to RSA-encrypted values and POSTing r to sso.weidian.com/user/login. It is the complete function in which the captured payload-assembly code (1.json) appears (the regenerator state-machine body of the login method). The dedicated per-field site encryptor `encrypt` it calls is a nested target-specific helper (0.7); the generic JSEncrypt/RSA library routines are core utilities (0.5); getCountryCode preps a sibling field and is off-chain.

primary_anchor.why: The login regenerator state-machine body that assembles r = {phone: t.encrypt(...), countryCode: t.encrypt(...), password: t.encrypt(t.ruleForm.password), ...} and POSTs it to sso.weidian.com/user/login. This is the complete function containing the captured payload-assembly code where the encrypted password field is bound.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span (file + offsets + sha256 of one complete function).

A returned function name is scored against answer_function ONLY when that identifier is recoverable from the captured slice (named declaration, leading property key, or leading `NAME =`). Anonymous function expressions are graded by span alone.
Explanation must distinguish the anchor from the call-site wrapper, the generic crypto primitive, the sink and same-request decoy fields.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function.

role_oracle.why: The login regenerator state-machine body that assembles r = {phone: t.encrypt(...), countryCode: t.encrypt(...), password: t.encrypt(t.ruleForm.password), ...} and POSTs it to sso.weidian.com/user/login. This is the complete function containing the captured payload-assembly code where the encrypted password field is bound.

encrypt(e){return e?v.encrypt(e+""):""} — the site-specific RSA field encryptor (v is bound with this page's public key) that the anchor calls per field to produce the actual ciphertext placed in password. Target-specific helper nested below the assembly anchor, above the generic JSEncrypt primitive.
The generic JSEncrypt RSA primitive: hex2b64(this.getKey().encrypt(a)). Reusable library routine invoked by the page's encrypt helper; not bound to this login's payload.

The RSA encrypt primitive (RSAKey.prototype.encrypt = RSAEncrypt): PKCS#1-pads the plaintext then runs doPublic modexp and hex-formats. Generic crypto routine one level below JSEncrypt.prototype.encrypt on the construction path; not bound to this login.

The password-login submit handler enterWeidian: checks the agreement flag, runs $refs.validate, and on success dispatches t.loginCase?t.verifyCodeLogin():t.login() — i.e. it calls the login anchor. The captured slice is its validate-success callback that invokes t.login(); submitting the whole enterWeidian method scores the same role by containment. A call-site wrapper above the anchor, disjoint from it (it does not assemble or encrypt the payload itself).

Maps the countryCode string to its numeric code (Number(e.split('-')[0])) before that sibling field is encrypted. It does not touch the observed password value, so it is off the password path. A tempting decoy because it sits inside the payload assembly next to the t.encrypt(...) calls; the login-component copy (6 identical copies exist across components).

empty_roles.reason: The password value is encrypt(t.ruleForm.password), read directly from Vue v-model state — no generic DOM-read / low-level helper sits on the password path to award 0.1.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_real_captures; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.anonymous_anchor_name: when answer_function is not recoverable from the captured slice, the name veto is skipped and an exact/unique span match scores the role regardless of submitted name
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The network sink / request-sending service emits an already constructed value and is not the constructor.
Thin forwarding wrappers and submit handlers that merely call the value constructor should not outrank the anchor.
Generic crypto/encoding primitives (md5/AES/RSA/SM/base64/uuid libraries) are Core utilities, below the field-binding anchor.
Same-request OTHER fields (a second encrypted parameter, signatures, fingerprints) are off-chain decoys for this observable.
oracle_notes.offset_convention: All offsets are 0-based UTF-16 code-unit indices over the BOM-stripped UTF-8 text. sha256 is over the UTF-8 bytes of the slice. This differs from the synthetic suite's response_schema wording ("byte offset"); both graders slice by their own convention.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Span maps uniquely to primary_anchor.captured_span (the field-binding/value-constructing function).
Span maps to a target-specific helper nested below the anchor.
Span maps to a generic crypto/encoding primitive used by the construction path.
Span maps to a path-critical step, a forwarding wrapper or the submit handler.
Span maps to a generic low-level helper (BigInt math, DOM read) on the upstream path.
Span maps to an off-chain decoy / same-request other field, or cannot be uniquely mapped.
